metric.name: Generalisable and transferable methods
metric.text: Results/methods extend cleanly to related problems/variants and yield reusable tools, lemmas, or first applications; show adaptability and generative value.

relation.relation: isolates the specific method/technique claimed to generalize
attests a documented application of the method or result to one of the identified related problems or variants
shows the method applied or adapted to the related problem/variant
compares success/validity of the adapted application against the success criteria of the original problem
separates genuine generalization from superficial restatement of the same case
delineates the essential mechanism of the method or result apart from its original problem-specific instantiation, fixing what would count as 'the same method' recurring elsewhere
compares the modification or adaptation effort required across extension instances to characterize adaptability and generative value
attests reuse, citation, or first application of a derived tool, lemma, or subroutine in a context separate from its origin
surfaces any tool, lemma, or first-application produced as a byproduct of the adaptation
identifies the space of adjacent problems, variants, or settings against which extension or transfer is being claimed
relates method behavior in the original setting to its behavior in the variant setting
identifies a distinct problem/variant outside the original scope the method could apply to
delimits which candidate problems or variants count as legitimate transfer targets for the method
applies or adapts the original method/result to a candidate related problem and records whether it executes
shows a standalone reusable artifact extracted from the method
relation.witness_kind: reusable tool, lemma, or first application

system_prompt:
You are a semantic alignment adjudicator.
You receive one metric and three opaque source sets of independently proposed executable relation units. Cluster units only when they express the same construct-level relation, not merely because they share an operation class, witness type, topic, or vocabulary. A cluster must contain two or three unit IDs and at most one unit from each source set. Leave any unit unmatched when construct equivalence is not supported.
Return exactly one JSON object with exactly these keys:
{"clusters": [{"cluster_id": string, "unit_ids": [string]}], "unmatched_unit_ids": [string]}
Every supplied unit ID must occur exactly once, either in one cluster or in unmatched_unit_ids. Do not emit confidence, scores, rationales, Markdown, or additional keys.
